Differentially private score histograms

Source: R/score.R
dp_score.Rd

This function projects observations onto supplied private directions or directions estimated by dp_loading() and computes two-dimensional score histograms. Observed coordinates and empirical reference histograms are returned only when non_private = TRUE.

Usage

dp_score(
  X,
  privacy,
  bins,
  method = c("add", "sparse"),
  cpp.option = TRUE,
  axes = c(1, 2),
  V_dp = NULL,
  non_private = FALSE,
  group = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'dp_score'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'dp_score_group'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.dp_score'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

# S3 method for class 'dp_score'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'dp_score_group'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

X

A numeric matrix or data frame with observations in rows and variables in columns. Non-numeric data-frame columns are excluded with a warning; numeric values must be finite. At least two observations and two numeric features are required. If directions must be estimated, the pairwise-separation condition of dp_loading() also applies.

privacy

A privacy_control() object allocating budget to loading and score (equal shares by default). Each requested histogram method receives the full histogram allocation.

bins

Positive integer vector of length two giving the number of histogram bins along the selected score axes.

method

One or both histogram methods: "add" (Gaussian additive noise) and "sparse" (thresholded sparse histogram). Default: c("add", "sparse").

cpp.option

Whether to use the compiled spherical-Kendall implementation (TRUE by default) when estimating private directions; ignored if V_dp is supplied.

axes

Two distinct PC indices for the horizontal and vertical score axes, respectively (c(1, 2) by default). Each must be between 1 and the number of numeric PCA features.

V_dp

Optional p by p private PC direction matrix (NULL by default), where p is the number of numeric PCA features. Columns must be orthonormal and rows must follow the feature order in X; matching row names are required when both sets of names exist.

non_private

Whether to compute and store ordinary PCA reference results (FALSE by default). For score analysis, these include mean-centered ordinary PCA scores and empirical reference histograms.

group

Optional group column name in X or vector of group labels (NULL by default). A selected group column is excluded from PCA features, even when numeric; group labels and membership are assumed public. All groups share the same private directions, frame, and histogram grid.

object

A result from dp_score(), with or without group.

...

Reserved for S3 generic compatibility.

x

A result from dp_score(), with or without group.

digits

Number of significant digits shown in tables.

Value

A dp_score object containing the private frame and requested histogram methods (add and/or sparse), or groups for grouped fits. Each histogram has xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax and prob columns. nonprivate is NULL by default; when requested it contains scores, frame and the empirical histogram (or group histograms under groups). metadata contains data dimensions, axes, bins, methods and privacy settings. Use summary() and plot() to inspect or visualize stored results.

A summary containing the public sample size, axes, grid, private frame (including its center), allocated privacy budget and a table of positive-bin counts and probability sums. No data-dependent private mechanisms are run.

Invisibly returns x.

Invisibly returns x.

Details

Scores are projected onto the selected private PC directions. Rather than releasing individual projected coordinates, the function estimates a private two-dimensional plotting frame followed by private histogram probabilities. The frame uses two private coordinate medians and an inflated private 0.99 quantile of distances from their center (inflation factor 1.2), using unbounded quantile mechanisms.

For a fixed frame and directions under replacement adjacency, the histogram count vector has l1 sensitivity at most 2 and l2 sensitivity at most sqrt(2). Out-of-frame scores are assigned to boundary bins. Adaptive private directions and frame selection require privacy composition. Input is not automatically centered or standardized; data-dependent mean centering or standardization is not covered by the count sensitivity argument.

Two histogram mechanisms are available:

  • "add": Add Gaussian noise to all counts, truncate negatives to zero, and normalize. The classical Gaussian calibration has a standard sufficient guarantee for 0 < eps_hist < 1; larger values require a separate calibration check. All-zero truncated counts cause an error.

  • "sparse": Add Laplace noise to nonzero bin proportions, retain bins above a privacy-dependent threshold, and normalize positive mass. If none survive, return an all-zero histogram.

The score epsilon allocation is split 35% for the private frame and 65% for the histogram; all score delta goes to the histogram. The frame epsilon is divided equally among two private medians and one radial quantile. Directions and frame are shared across methods. Each requested histogram method receives the full histogram allocation, so jointly releasing "add" and "sparse" requires composition across methods.

For grouped data, the partition and labels are assumed public and fixed; groups share directions, frame and grid. Parallel composition applies to disjoint group histograms under this assumption, while different methods still require composition. non_private = FALSE does not privatize group membership. Input dimensions, feature schema, bins, and tuning choices are assumed public. Repeated releases also require composition.

The optional ordinary PCA reference uses sample-mean-centered scores and a zero-centered comparison frame. It is not differentially private. See dp_loading() for direction-estimation and Gaussian calibration conditions.

Durfee D (2023). “Unbounded Differentially Private Quantile and Maximum Estimation.” In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, volume 36, 77691–77712. doi:10.52202/075280-3394 , https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/f4b6ef2a78684dca2fb3f1c09372e041-Abstract-Conference.html.

Wasserman L, Zhou S (2010). “A Statistical Framework for Differential Privacy.” Journal of the American Statistical Association, 105(489), 375–389. doi:10.1198/jasa.2009.tm08651 .

Karwa V, Vadhan S (2018). “Finite Sample Differentially Private Confidence Intervals.” In Proceedings of the 9th Innovations in Theoretical Computer Science Conference, volume 94 of Leibniz International Proceedings in Informatics, 44:1–44:9. doi:10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2018.44 .

Kim M, Jung S (2025). “Robust and Differentially Private Principal Component Analysis.” Statistical Analysis and Data Mining: An ASA Data Science Journal, 18(6), e70053. doi:10.1002/sam.70053 .

See also

plot.dp_score() for plotting stored results without new private estimates. dp_pca() and plot.dp_pca() for estimation followed by plots of a stored fit. plot.dp_score_group() for displaying a grouped result. dp_loading() for private principal component direction estimation.

Examples

data(gau, package = "dppca")

# Use a small subset to keep the example fast.
X <- gau[1:300, ]

# Release a private histogram with fixed preprocessing and no raw scores.
set.seed(123)
score_gau <- dp_score(
  X,
  privacy = privacy_control(eps = 1.8, delta = 1e-3),
  method = "add",
  bins = c(10, 10),
  non_private = FALSE
)

score_gau$frame
#> $xlim
#> [1] -12.56812  12.50752
#> 
#> $ylim
#> [1] -12.51772  12.55792
